newsitem.title: GERMANY: German inflation remains subdued in April.
newsitem.headline: German inflation remains subdued in April.

text.p: German inflation remained subdued in April, eliminating worries prompted by an upturn earlier this year, preliminary data released by the Federal Statistics Office showed on Thursday.
Bundesbank council member Krupp said there was no need to worry about price pressures at this time.

Asked whether the recent depreciation of the mark had been weathered without increasing inflationary risks in Germany, Krupp said "that depends on how the economy develops. It is hard to assess. The information we have so far shows no need for concern on the price front."
Consumer prices in west Germany fell 0.1 percent from last month, and were only 1.4 percent above the year-earlier level. In March, west German prices had risen 1.6 percent from a year before.
"The data is lower than expected," said economist Holger Fahrinkrug at UBS in Frankfurt. "There is no price pressure and much of the increase at the beginning of the year was seasonal."
Fahrinkrug said the data change the medium-term outlook, eliminating any sign of an upward trend in inflation, and that he expected inflation to average 1.5 percent for the year.

Despite the recent weakness of the mark, which is flashing alarm signals to some economists, weak domestic demand has prevented companies from passing along higher import costs to consumers, Fahrinkrug said.
West German inflation has remained comfortably below two percent since April 1995, though it bubbled up to 1.9 percent in January of this year.

Mathias Haffner of BZW in Frankfurt said unless the dollar goes through the roof, which he is not expecting, he sees no inflation danger in the near-term. The new data should not change the Bundesbank interest rate outlook, he said.
Final data for April, reflecting prices nationwide as well as the regional breakdown, will be released in mid-May.
